sent_subject: Nook Sleep tracking teardown: event map + coupon‑source plan
sent:
Naomi —

Here’s the 1‑page teardown you asked for.

What’s noisy now
- Three discount paths on Classic (AUTUMN40 banner, 5% email, 10% SMS) + two CTAs (“Add to Basket”, “Buy Now”) + a quiz/compare link. Great UX, hard attribution.

Event map to make it measurable
Define one source‑of‑truth event: purchase (or first_order) with these properties:
- promo_source: seasonal_autumn40 | email_welcome5 | sms_join10 | none
- checkout_path: buy_now | add_to_cart
- product_family: classic | hybrid | luxe
- size: single | double | king | super_king
- pillows_added: true/false
- delivery_band: next_day | 2_5_days | 3_7_days (from postcode estimate)
- finance_selected: true/false (Klarna)
Up‑funnel events to feed diagnostics:
- quiz_started / quiz_completed (from Not sure? Take the quiz), compare_opened
- size_selected, postcode_checked, add_pillows_clicked
- add_to_cart, buy_now_clicked
- coupon_applied with coupon_code and inferred promo_source
Echo promo_source and checkout_path onto purchase so reports tie back.

Quick fixes (no redesign)
- Distinct tagging: set promo_source when a visitor enters via each path:
  - URL param on the AUTUMN40 banner links (e.g. ?promo=autumn40) sets coupon field and promo_source=seasonal_autumn40.
  - Email/SMS links set promo_source=email_welcome5 or sms_join10 regardless of the code used.
- Pre-apply vs manual: capture whether the code was auto‑applied or typed; shoppers who type borrowed codes behave differently.
- Split CTAs: attach checkout_path=buy_now or add_to_cart at click, and persist it through checkout into purchase.
- Delivery promise: when postcode returns next-day, set delivery_band=next_day immediately and carry it to purchase; you can later test surfacing that promise earlier.
- One purchase signal: ensure only one purchase fires per order with stable event_id for dedup across pixels and server events.

Cross‑domain/checkout checklist (use if any step leaves your domain)
- Keep the same user/session identifiers across domains; pass click IDs through checkout and back to the thank‑you page.
- Send server‑side purchase with the same event_id as the client event.
- Pass coupon_code, promo_source, and checkout_path on every checkout step so failure states don’t lose the trail.

Why this matters
- You’ll be able to compare discount paths side‑by‑side (“seasonal vs email vs SMS”) and see which one drives first orders at the best cost, not just which one gets used most.
- When you do move paid traffic onto single‑promise offer pages, the purchase event already knows which promise and path won.

If you want, I’ll add a one‑pager showing how we turned this into cleaner cost‑per‑first‑order decisions on a food DTC brand.
